data.title: Crane Company to Acquire Trillium U.S. Pump Business
data.description:
The latest update is out from Crane Company ( (CR) ).

On September 14, 2026, Crane Company announced it had entered into a definitive agreement to acquire the U.S. pump business of First Reserve-backed Trillium Flow Technologies for approximately $240 million, valuing the target at about 14.6 times estimated 2026 adjusted EBITDA. The business, which expects full-year revenue of roughly $115 million and is slated to close in the fourth quarter subject to customary approvals, includes well-known brands such as Floway, Wemco, Roto-Jet, and WSP that provide mission-critical pumping solutions for municipal water and wastewater markets.

Crane’s management said the deal will strengthen the company’s Process Flow Technologies segment by expanding its presence in highly engineered pump technologies and increasing exposure to resilient water and wastewater end markets. The acquired operation brings a large installed base that supports recurring service, repair, retrofit, and replacement demand, positioning Crane to drive aftermarket growth and product innovation by integrating these brands with its operating system and commercial capabilities.

data.title: Mako Mining Signs LOI for Long-Term Gold Stream with Sailfish to Cut Capital Costs
data.description:
Mako Mining Corp ( (TSE:MKO) ) has provided an announcement.

Mako Mining Corp. announced on September 14, 2026 that it signed a non-binding letter of intent, dated September 11, 2026, with Sailfish Royalty Corp. for a corporate-level, long-term gold stream intended to lower its cost of capital. The proposed agreement would see Mako deliver increasing monthly volumes of refined gold over a 240‑month term, in exchange for Sailfish paying a fixed percentage of the London Bullion Market Association gold price and issuing 70 million Sailfish shares, which would leave Mako holding roughly 49% of Sailfish.

Management says the transaction is designed to exploit the valuation and cost-of-capital advantages of royalty vehicles, positioning Sailfish shares as a strategic financing currency and enabling larger, potentially accretive acquisitions or substantial dividend distributions. The deal, which is a related-party transaction due to common control by Wexford Capital, is subject to a definitive gold purchase agreement, security over key Mako assets, independent valuation, minority shareholder approval and regulatory sign-offs, with no assurance it will be completed on the proposed terms.
